name: Vilhelm Hammershøi
bio: Vilhelm Hammershøi, often anglicised as Vilhelm Hammershoi, was a Danish painter. He is known for his poetic, subdued portraits and interiors. In 1905, Rainer Maria Rilke wrote of the artist, "Hammershøi is not one of those about whom one can speak quickly. His work is wide-ranging and slow, and at whatever moment one comprehends it, it will always provide an opportunity to talk about what is important and essential in art".

paintings.title: Amalienborg Square, Copenhagen
paintings.story: Amalienborg Square, Copenhagen is an 1896 oil-on-canvas painting by the Danish artist Vilhelm Hammershøi in the Statens Museum for Kunst.

paintings.title: Støvkornenes dans i solstrålerne
paintings.story: Støvkornenes dans i solstrålerne, also Solstråler, is an oil painting from 1900 by the Danish Symbolist painter Vilhelm Hammershøi. Considered to be one of the masterpieces of Danish culture, it was included in the 2006 Danish Culture Canon.
facts: When he exhibited the painting, Hammershøi called it Solskin (sunshine) or Solstråler (sunbeams).
It was only later it was given the more poetic title of Støvkornenes dans i solstrålerne.

paintings.title: Interior with an Easel, Bredgade 25
paintings.story: Interior with an Easel, Bredgade 25 is an oil-on-canvas painted by Danish artist Vilhelm Hammershøi in 1912. It was acquired by the Getty Museum, in Los Angeles, in 2018. The painting depicts the artist's apartment at Bredgade 25 in Copenhagen, which was his address up to his death in 1916.
facts: Another variant, which was undated features a chair but with a covered porcelain bowl in the background, was featured at a Sotheby's auction in 1975.
Hammershøi is renowned for his sense of minimalism and his color palettes which consist of muted neutral colors, which consist of greys, desaturated yellows, greens, etc.

paintings.title: Interior with Young Woman Seen from the Back
paintings.story: Interior with Young Woman Seen from the Back is an oil-on-canvas painting from c. 1903–04 by the Danish artist Vilhelm Hammershøi. It is now held in the Randers Museum of Art. It uses the muted grey-blue palette, uncluttered composition and detailed attention to the play of light typical of Hammershøi's work.
facts: The young woman featured is Hammershøi's wife, Ida, whom he painted frequently with her back turned.

Michael Palin, an admirer of Hammershøi's work, believes that Ida is often depicted facing away since, in the portraits in which she is facing the viewer, her face reveals "a troubled soul"; and that maybe Hammershøi painted her in structured, minimalist interiors as a response to an emotionally fraught domestic life.

paintings.title: Ida Reading a Letter
paintings.story: Ida Reading a Letter is an 1899 oil-on-canvas painting by the Danish artist Vilhelm Hammershøi. It is an example of a work inspired by Dutch Golden Age painting and is currently in a private collection.
facts: This painting seems to have been directly inspired by a Vermeer he must have seen in Amsterdam, Woman in Blue Reading a Letter.
In 1887, Hammershoi travelled to the Netherlands, where he saw first-hand works by Dutch 17th-century master Johannes Vermeer and his Delft contemporaries.

paintings.title: Interior with a Reading Lady
paintings.story: This is usually the kind of painting we associate with Vilhelm Hammershøi; pictures of sparsely furnished rooms. Occasionally, a woman reading or simply being in the room, often with her back turned. The artist conjures up a charged atmosphere using small means – light, shadow, space, walls and doorways. Even if the painting actually depicts the artist’s home, the rooms have a timeless character. A place for memories and imagination.

paintings.title: Landscape, From Lejre
paintings.story: Vilhelm Hammershøi’s landscapes often, as here, lack people. Instead his vision is focused on a few prominent features – the curved shapes of the fields, echoed by the rounded hills and verdant copses. Together with the white summer clouds, the landscape offers a sense of unimpeded, billowing rhythm. In 1905 Hammershøi painted a series of landscapes from the district of Lejre on Zealand in Denmark, which included this painting.

paintings.title: Interior
paintings.story: A solitary woman in a sparsely furnished room is a recurring theme in Hammershøi’s pictures. The light comes from the side, and the figure often has her back to the viewer. Clear models for these interiors can be found in 17th-century Holland or early 19th- century Denmark. But Hammershøi’s silent, empty rooms also have an intense, suggestive mood all their own. Most of his interior scenes were painted in his home in Copenhagen, but this one was executed in London. The model is the artist’s wife Ida.

paintings.title: A room. The corner of a room with walls painted grey-lilac, divided into panels.
paintings.story: The full description of the painting is: Stue. Hjørnet af en Stue med graa-lilla Vægge, inddelte i Felter. Paa Bagvæggen en hvid Dør, paa Sidevæggen tilhøjre en anden do. Imellem de to, i Hjørnet, en Kakkelovn med langt Rør. Længst fremme et Spillebord, ved hvilket en sortklædt Kvinde sidder og syer. (A room. The corner of a room with walls painted grey-lilac, divided into panels. At the back a white door, and on the right wall another one. Between the two, in the corner, a masonry heater with a long pipe. At the front a gambling table, where a woman is sitting, sewing.). The description is from Michaelis and Bramsen's list of paintings by Hammershøi. They gave it number 173, indicating that it was painted in 1897. The contemporary expert Poul Vad dismissed this, as the interior is from Strandgade 30 in Copenhagen, where the Hammerhøi family lived from September 1898 to 1909. So the date of the painting would be in that period.

paintings.title: Study showing the back of a boy.
paintings.story: The experts at Bruun Rasmussen saw this as a study from Hammershøi's time as pupil in Krøyer's school of painting. They referred to a similar painting from around 1884, probably of the same young man.

paintings.title: Young forest. Trørød
paintings.story: Trørød is a village in North Zealand where Hammershøi spent time in the summer of 1907.

paintings.title: Dunkebakke, Frederiksværk
paintings.story: Dunkebakke is a hill outside the Danish town of Frederiksværk. Hammershøi spent the summer of 1904 in Arresødal, near Frederiksværk and he finished the painting in September of that year.

paintings.title: Room (Ida in an interior)
paintings.story: The desciption given in Michaëlis and Bramsen, Vilhelm Hammershøi, kunstneren og hans værk, 1918, page 94: Tilvenstre en Sofa med grønligt Betræk. I Midten et Mahogni Spillebord. En sortklædt Kvinde støtter sin højre Haand paa Bordet, den venstre paa en Stol. I baggrunden et Fyrretræs Skab. Tilhøjre paa Gulvet en Bindesbøllsk Krukke. ("To the left a sofa with green upholstery. In the middle a mahogany card table. A woman dressed in black resting her right hand on the table, her left on a chair. In the background a pinewood closet. To the right, on the floor, a jar of the Bindesbøll type.") Source at kunstbib.dk

paintings.title: View from Frederiksholms Kanal, Copenhagen.
paintings.story: The view in this painting was from the home of Hammershøi's friend and benefactor Alfred Bramsen, who lived on the corner of Stormgade and Frederiksholms Kanal in Copenhagen. The dark building to the left is Staldmestergaarden, and the tall red building is Materielgaarden. The scenery was seen in November on a misty and overcast day.
